AI Adoption and Employment Expectations: Evidence from a Survey of Small Business Owners
Economy-wide measures of pay and headcount have moved little even as AI adoption has spread rapidly, yet narrower measures document declining hiring for workers at the start of their careers or in AI-exposed occupations . In this post, we revisit this topic for U.S. small businesses.
We use data from the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey (SBCS) to examine the twelve-month-forward employment and revenue expectations of AI users.
AI Use by Large and Small Businesses
AI may be particularly helpful for small firms in dealing with operational challenges such as hiring, marketing, and technology-related issues.
Summing Up
This suggests that AI may be helping some small businesses overcome specific operational or technical constraints that limit revenue generation, rather than simply reflecting broad-based optimism or expectations of expansion through hiring.

Which businesses are using AI technology?
Posted on October 19, 2026
SHARE THIS PAGE: Link Copied
The takeaway
According to the Ramp AI Index, as of September 2026, more than half of all businesses paid for an artificial intelligence (AI) product or service. Adoption rates jumped in the months after ChatGPT's public launch in late 2022 and have risen steadily since.
The data
Adoption by business size : AI adoption has climbed for businesses of every size, although it is spreading fastest at bigger and medium-sized companies. Adoption among small-sized businesses has grown steadily, but they lag the other two groups.
Adoption by industry : Industry matters much more than size.
The information sector, which includes software and publishing, has consistently recorded the highest adoption rates since 2023, with finance and insurance close behind. Other industries, in decreasing order of AI adoption are manufacturing, retail trade, health care and social assistance, construction, and accommodation and food services.
Adoption by provider : A business can pay for AI products and services offered by more than one provider, so the adoption shares reported by Ramp don't match the overall adoption rate. OpenAI surged in the first months of 2023 and kept rising through most of 2025, but it has leveled off since then. Anthropic gained ground steadily from 2024 on.

Discussion Paper
AI Adoption and Employment Expectations: Evidence from a Survey of Small Business Owners
Abstract: There is little consensus on the effect of AI adoption on employment. Economy-wide measures of pay and headcount have moved little even as AI adoption has spread rapidly, yet narrower measures document declining hiring for workers at the start of their careers or in AI-exposed occupations. In this post, we revisit this topic for U.S.
small businesses. We use data from the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey (SBCS) to examine the twelve-month-forward employment and revenue expectations of AI users.
We find that firms currently using AI are significantly more likely than non-users to expect increased employment and revenues over the next year, even after accounting for firm and owner characteristics and location. Revenue expectations are most optimistic for AI users that report facing operational challenges in utilizing technology.

NY Fed: Small Firms Using AI Expect More Sales and Hiring
By Trevor Fenner
NY Fed: Small Firms Using AI Expect More Sales and Hiring
NY Fed: Small Firms Using AI Expect More Sales and Hiring
Affiliate disclosure: This post contains affiliate links. If you buy through them, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Full disclosure
Small businesses that use AI expect stronger sales and hiring over the next year than those that don’t, according to a New York Fed survey published October 8.
If you run a store, that sentence will tempt you to buy more AI tools or hire fewer people. Hold off on both until you see what the survey measured.
Will Aarons and Asani Sarkar of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published the analysis on October 8 on the bank’s Liberty Street Economics blog . They used the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, fielded September to November 2025. The AI module covers 5,248 employer firms, weighted to match the national population of employer firms.
Per the post, 46% of firms with at least one employee said they or their employees were using AI tools, and another 15% planned to adopt within twelve months. Among the users, 63% called AI somewhat or very important to production, and 51% had integrated it partially or fully into business processes.
Bloomberg reported in September 2024 that AI adopters weren’t slashing jobs in an earlier NY Fed survey. Two years on, the pattern is still retraining and slower hiring more than mass cuts.
They measure different things. The Census Bureau survey covers all businesses and reworded its question in November 2025, while the NY Fed survey covers employer firms with at least one worker. A Federal Reserve Board note attributes most gaps to sampling, units of measurement and question wording.

Are Businesses Scaling Back Hiring Due to AI?
Businesses reported a notable increase in AI use over the past year, yet very few firms reported AI-induced layoffs. Indeed, for those already employed, our results indicate AI is more likely to result in retraining than job loss, similar to our findings from last year .
More Businesses Are Using AI
Our August business surveys asked firms in the New York–Northern New Jersey region whether they used AI as part of their business process in the past six months and whether they planned to use AI over the next six months. This included searching for information, marketing, business analytics, data management, and customer service, among other uses.
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Regional Business Surveys, August 2025. Note: Firms using AI exclusively as an information search tool but nothing else were not counted as AI users.
As might be expected, AI use varied widely among businesses in different industries.

New York Fed Finds Small Businesses Using AI Expect More Hiring and Revenue
In a survey of more than 5,000 employer firms, 46% said they use AI, and most said it has not changed their labor costs.
Filed October 12, 2026 The Emerging Tech How To desk
Researchers Will Aarons and Asani Sarkar at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York published new findings on October 8 on the bank's Liberty Street Economics blog .
They analyzed the AI questions in the Federal Reserve Banks' 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, which covered 5,248 U.S. firms with at least one employee.
Adoption is broad: 46% of employer firms said their business or employees use AI tools, and another 15% planned to start within a year.
Among AI users, 63% said AI was somewhat or very important to how they produce their goods or services.
So far the payoff shows up more in sales than in savings. 31% of AI users reported higher sales from AI, while 77% said AI had not changed their labor costs.
AI users were also more optimistic about the year ahead, both on adding employees and on revenue, than firms that do not use AI. The gap narrowed but held after the researchers controlled for firm and owner characteristics.
* AI Adoption and Employment Expectations: Evidence from a Survey of Small Business Owners (Federal Reserve Bank of New York)

In a New York Fed analysis of the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, 46% of employer firms used AI. AI users had a net 33 percentage point expectation of adding staff over the next year, against 15 points for non-users, and the gap held after controls.

Why it matters. Most US jobs are at small firms; their AI plans may matter more for hiring than big-company announcements.
Small US businesses that use AI are more likely to expect to hire over the next year than those that do not, according to a New York Fed analysis published on 8 October on its Liberty Street Economics blog.
The numbers
Economists Will Aarons and Asani Sarkar used the 2025 Small Business Credit Survey, whose AI module covered 5,248 employer firms. Of these, 46% said they use AI tools and another 15% planned to adopt them within 12 months.
Among AI users, the share expecting employment to rise minus the share expecting it to fall was 33 percentage points.
The gap was largest among firms in fair or poor financial condition: 21 points on employment and 24 on revenue.
Student Small firms adopting AI are the ones planning to hire; skills with those tools help.

Professional AI use so far has not changed labour costs for most small firms, the survey found.
